question: Can reported central-bank gold buying be used ex ante as a direct XAU/USD trading signal?

facts.source: World Gold Council Gold Reserves by Country
facts.finding: Monthly files are normally updated during the first ten days of the month with data two months in arrears; late reporters can be older and known corrections supplement IMF IFS.

facts.source: World Gold Council Central Bank Gold Reserves Survey 2026 methodology
facts.finding: The intentions survey is annual, voluntary and anonymous; 2026 fieldwork ran from 5 February to 19 May and aggregated 76 eligible responses.
COFER is quarterly, voluntary and reports foreign-exchange reserves rather than monetary gold; individual-country currency allocations remain confidential.

operational_rule: An agent may use point-in-time official-flow releases to describe a slow regime from their actual publication date onward. It must not align purchases to the economic month as if known then, trigger short-horizon entries, or rescue a failed price strategy post hoc.
why_it_matters: A backtest aligned to the month being reported would leak roughly two months of future information and manufacture an unrealistically timely relationship.
relationship_to_cftc_v32: This audit covers central-bank reserve reporting. CFTC positioning is a separate, timelier dataset and remains blocked on its own publication ledger rather than rejected by this finding.
next: Retain central-bank flow only as slow point-in-time context; keep the separate CFTC release-ledger gate unchanged.
